description: Focal search (A*ε) finds a path that costs at most `w` times the optimum (it is *bounded-suboptimal*). It keeps the open states ordered by `f = g + h`, where `h` is *admissible*: it never overestimates the remaining cost. The *focal list* holds the open states with `f ≤ w · f_min`, where `f_min` is the smallest `f` that is open. Focal search expands the focal state with the smallest value of a second, free *focal key*, which in the crate may depend on the whole path, for example the number of conflicts in multi-agent path finding. With `w = 1` it is A* that breaks ties by the focal key.

papers.title: Studies in Semi-Admissible Heuristics
papers.venue: IEEE Transactions on Pattern Analysis and Machine Intelligence
